rationale: Tests the critical distinction between diarrhoea and dysentery that determines all downstream triage—anchored after the definitions block.
Tests understanding of cholera toxin's molecular mechanism which explains the purely secretory, non-bloody nature of cholera stool—anchored after the V. cholerae pathogenesis block.
Tests the pathognomonic microscopic criterion for confirming E. histolytica—a core MI4.4 skill—anchored after the amoebic dysentery block.
Tests recall of Rotavirus structure and epidemiology—the most important viral cause of severe infant diarrhoea in India—anchored after the viral diarrhoea block.
Tests visual recognition of organism microscopy matched to characteristic stool macroscopic appearance—a core laboratory identification skill—anchored after the practical lab diagnosis block.
Tests application of the three-type food poisoning classification to a clinical scenario—anchored after the classification block establishing intoxication vs toxico-infection vs infection.
Myth-busts the dangerous assumption that reheating contaminated cream foods prevents staphylococcal food poisoning—anchored after the S. aureus food poisoning block.
Tests organism-food-toxin association in the classic reheated fried rice scenario—anchored after the block covering B. cereus and other food poisoning agents.
Tests understanding of urease as the key survival mechanism enabling H. pylori colonisation of the acidic stomach—anchored after the pathogenesis block.
Tests clinical application of diagnostic test selection for H. pylori eradication confirmation—anchored after the comprehensive diagnostic modalities block.
Corrects the misconception that all H. pylori strains are equally carcinogenic—anchored after the CagA clinical pearl establishing variable virulence.
Tests clinical application of HEV diagnosis in the high-mortality pregnancy scenario—anchored after the HEV block establishing the critical third-trimester fatality risk.
Tests recall of HBV serological marker meanings—the foundation for all subsequent serological interpretation—anchored after the HBV structure and markers block.
Tests understanding of age-dependent chronicity risk—the key reason vertical transmission prevention is the highest priority—anchored after the HBV pathogenesis block.
Tests recall of HCV's uniquely high chronicity rate—the key clinical differentiator among hepatitis viruses—anchored after the HCV/HDV block.
Tests interpretation of post-vaccination serology—a core skill for health worker screening—anchored after the vaccination and post-exposure prophylaxis block.
Tests integration of multiple HBV markers to interpret a complex serological panel—anchored after the window period clinical pearl completing the serology interpretation concept.
